title: Cart and checkout API
idea: The cart API exposes the cart, checkout and orders as REST resources; checkout runs in one transaction and accepts an Idempotency-Key so retries are safe.

analogy.text: A pharmacy counter. The assistant checks the prescription is readable, the pharmacist decides what can be dispensed, and the stockroom only fetches boxes.
analogy.breaks: A pharmacist may phone a doctor; the service never calls out mid-transaction.

points: Repeating a `PUT` or `DELETE` on a cart item leaves the same cart state.
`POST /checkout` sends the total the shopper saw; a mismatch returns 409.
A repeated Idempotency-Key returns the stored order with 200, not a new one.
One error middleware maps validation, domain and duplicate errors to status codes.

code.title: Layered checkout route
code.caption: Repository, service, controller and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. The user id comes from a header here; real apps read it from auth. This trimmed version skips the order_item copy; page 6 shows it.

walk.text: Trimmed schema and seed: U-7's cart holds two mugs and a T-shirt; U-9 wants the same T-shirt.
`tx` gives each service call one transaction and rolls back on any throw.
Repository: plain SQL, including the conditional UPDATE that reserves stock.
Replay a known key first; then refuse an empty cart or a changed total.
Reserve each line, create the order PENDING_PAYMENT, and empty the cart.
The controller demands the key, parses with `zod`, and picks 201 or 200.
Error middleware maps each error type to a status; Express 5 forwards async throws here.

pitfalls: Never call the payment provider inside the checkout transaction; row locks stay held while you wait.
Scope Idempotency-Key lookups to the user, or one shopper could replay another's order.
Do not return 500 for empty stock; 409 tells the client to refresh the cart.

quiz.q: What status does U-7's last POST /checkout print?
quiz.why: The previous k-1 request created OR-1. The last one finds it by user and key, returns it unchanged, and the controller marks a replay with 200.

takeaway: Validate in the controller, decide in one transaction, replay safely by Idempotency-Key.
